As a solution to this problem, the episode guide confirmed that the Jedi actually ''knew'' Maul's identity and suggested that the name of the Sith Lord was leaked by the captured Neimoidians after the Battle of Naboo.{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode314.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Witches of the Mist}} Despite his popularity and striking appearance, Maul made only a few appearances in official materials after the release of ''The Phantom Menace''. However, after he was revealed to have survived on [[George Lucas]]'s order{{InsiderCite|134|Behind and Beyond the Battle Lines}} in ''Witches of the Mist'', various new materials were released such as ''[[Restraint]]'', ''[[The Wrath of Darth Maul]]'', and [[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]. These fleshed out Maul's backstory more than ever before. However, the ''The Clone Wars'' epiosde ''[[Monster]]'' [[Retroactive continuity|changed]] his species from Zabrak{{DB|character|darthmaul|Maul, Darth|oldversion=20101109173652}} to Dathomirian,{{TCW|Monster}} a Human-Zabrak hybrid species.{{InsiderCite|122|Everything You Always Wanted to Know about the Nightsisters but Were Afraid to Ask}} ''Monster'' also shows all the Nightbrothers with tattoos resembling Maul's and ''Darth Plagueis'' describes Maul as having tattoos when Sidious meets him, [[Canon|decanonizing]] flashbacks in ''Marked'' that show Sidious meeting a tattoo-less Maul and Sidious applying Maul's tattoos. Maul's bipedal cyborg body was partially derived from his appearance in the non-canon comic ''[[Old Wounds]]''.{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/revenge-episode-guide|text="Revenge" Episode Guide | The Clone Wars}} In his ''Clone Wars'' appearances, beginning in Spring [[2012]], Maul was voiced by [[Sam Witwer]].{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/article/2011/10/12/star-wars-clone-wars-darth-maul|text=Darth Maul Lives! 'Star Wars: The Clone Wars' shows his life after vivisection|author=Christian Blauvelt|date=2011-10-12|format=Interview with [[Dave Filoni]]|language=English|archivedate=20200520012626}} [[File:Damage.jpg|225px|thumb|right|Concept art of ''Battle of the Sith Lords'', featuring Darth Maul]] A video game, tentatively called ''[[Battle of the Sith Lords]]'', was developed by [[Red Fly Studio]] before being cancelled. It would have revived Maul for the [[Legacy era]], striking out against Darth Krayt's army alongside Darth Talon.{{WebCite|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2015/10/26/the-story-of-the-darth-maul-game-that-never-came-to-be.aspx|text=The Story Of The Darth Maul Game That Never Came To Be|author=Reiner, Andrew|date=2015-10-26|work=GameInformer|archivedate=20200320000537}} After the Expanded Universe was reclassified as [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] in [[2014]], Maul's fate in the ''Legends'' continuity has been left uncertain, though his canon counterpart's story arc, and enmity with [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], were concluded in the ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' episode "[[Twin Suns (episode)|Twin Suns]]." ===Release information=== {{Quote|You worms are no match for the dark side!|Darth Maul|''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''}} The duel between Darth Maul and Qui-Gon Jinn on Tatooine and the duel with the two Jedi in Theed are featured in the [[Star Wars video games|video game]]s [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]] ([[1999]]), ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles]]'' (1999), and ''[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']] ([[2002]]). The duel in ''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'' contradicts that of the movie. Kenobi fights Darth Maul until he reduces the latter's health, then cuts his lightsaber in half. Then the duel resumes until Kenobi emerges victorious, slicing into Maul then Force-pushing him into the pit. The sequence omits Kenobi being knocked into the pit. In [[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga|the LEGO video game]], Darth Maul takes the form of a LEGO minifigure to fight the heroes of the saga. After his final duel, his torso falls into the pit, but his lower legs remain where he stood and even move around as if still attached to his body. During the planning stages of ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'', which was released in [[2008]], Darth Maul was one of the characters being considered to have his own game centered around him. Instead, he was given a cameo as one of PROXY's training holograms.''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'' [[Celebration IV]] presentation He also makes a non-canon appearance in [[Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3]] as a secret unlockable character. Maul is a playable character in ''Star Wars Battlefront 2''. Darth Maul was featured in two "Evolution" three-packs from [[Hasbro]]. One was entitled ''The Sith Legacy'', where Maul was alongside [[Darth Nihilus]] and [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]]. In the other, entitled ''The Sith'', Maul was alongside Count Dooku and Palpatine. ===Non-canon content=== Darth Maul is a favorite subject for [[Infinities|non-canon]], what-if stories. He was first "resurrected" in [[Star Wars Tales 9|''Star Wars Tales'' 9]], where he fought Darth Vader in the short ''Infinities'' story "[[Resurrection (comic story)|Resurrection]]," though it was never made clear in the story how this Maul was resurrected. [[Leland Chee]] later declared that the incident was canon, without clarifying the origins of this entity.{{Blog|holocron|22|Movie Characters killed in the EU}} In July [[2018]], the author of "Resurrection", [[Ron Marz]], stated on his [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]] account that "Maul was real in context of the story."{{Twitter|ronmarz|status/1021913683214127105|Ron Marz|quote=Maul was real in context of the story.|archivedate=20210308202250}} He then elaborated that "I can say for certain Maul was real. Because I made it all up."{{Twitter|ronmarz|status/1024143622424473600|Ron Marz|quote=I can say for certain Maul was real. Because I made it all up.|archivedate=20210308202224}} A common gag in ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga|LEGO Star Wars]]'' material was for Maul to appear in sequences in which he would not normally belong, such as appearing when the theme "[[Duel of the Fates]]" was used in association with [[Jek-14/Legends|Jek-14]] to complain that he "stole his theme song."''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Yoda Chronicles]]'' - "[[Menace of the Sith]]" {{Noncanonstart|legends=1}} ====Early life==== [[File:Maul_Hoverboard.jpg|thumb|left|A young Maul steals a [[Skimboard/Legends|skimboard]] from a bystander.]] During Maul's early years, he was sent to the [[Happy Nerf Herder]], a maximum security home for wayward boys on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. While there, he was involved in a breakout and, upon escaping, went on a hunt for a lollipop. After using a cable to get to the nearby [[Mon Calamari Fish Market]], Maul stole a [[Skimboard/Legends|hoverboard]] from a bystander, accidentally causing an explosion by doing so. He used this hoverboard to get to the [[RIB hutt]], restaurant where he stole a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] from a Jedi who was at the establishment. Maul used this lightsaber to descend the building. Though the Jedi chased him, Maul eventually landed upon a [[Granite slug/Legends|granite slug]] and onto an air taxi, catapulting both Maul and the slug onto a nearby building which contained a lollipop shop. Before Maul was able to obtain his sought-after lollipop, however, he was taken captive by a [[Senate Guard/Legends|Senate Guard]] who brought him before [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]. Though the Guardsman wanted to take him back to the home, Palpatine stated that Maul simply needed better guidance, and that he would re-educate the boy personally. ====Hunting Obi-Wan==== [[File:DarthMaul-Visionaries.png|thumb|right|150px|Darth Maul, returned from the dead, surviving thanks to a [[Cybernetics/Legends|prosthetic lower half]]]] {{Quote|There is no Palpatine. No Empire. No Jedi. There is no light, no dark… just you and I here now.|Darth Maul, to Obi-Wan Kenobi|{{StoryCite|story=Old Wounds|book=Star Wars: Visionaries}}}} After the Clone Wars, Maul hunted Obi-Wan Kenobi for many years, always being but a step behind him until [[16 BBY/Legends|16 BBY]] when he discovered [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen Lars]] and a young [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]. He [[Duel at the Lars homestead|attacked]] them while still staying in his hooded cloak, his [[Wikipedia:digitigrade|digitigrade]] droid legs the only part of him visible to others. He proceeded to call out through the Force to an unseen enemy he could nevertheless sense. The evil, psychic voice claimed to have been tracking this ancient adversary for years, just missing him on his missions to [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]], and [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]] and to have killed many witnesses on [[Polis Massa/Legends|Polis Massa]] before finally gaining crucial information in [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] from an [[Watto/Legends|aged Toydarian junk dealer]], whom he then murdered. The dark creature declared that he knew threatening Luke Skywalker would bring his adversary out into the open. At this point, a gray-haired Ben Kenobi resolved from the sand and confronted Maul, provoking the former Sith to cast aside his cloak and reveal his identity. With his severed lower body replaced by a pair of large cybernetic legs and abdomen, and his cranial horns having grown to over three times their original length, Maul was consumed with greater hatred than ever before and clearly never resumed contact with his former master, having dedicated his new life to avenging himself on the man who had bested him. [[File:OvMVisionaries.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Maul and Kenobi rematch.]] Kenobi and Maul engaged in a furious rematch. Kenobi managed to gain the upper hand when he severed Maul's right arm, cutting the darksider's weapon in two in the process, as well as breaking several of Maul's horns with his bare hand. Maul summoned the remaining half of his weapon and turned to face Kenobi, only to find himself facing the Jedi's lightsaber emitter. Kenobi hesitated to execute his helpless opponent, but had the decision taken out of his hands when the revived Owen killed Maul with his damaged rifle. Obi-Wan said he would take the body and burn it in the [[Dune Sea/Legends|Dune Sea]]; Owen told Kenobi that Luke would be safer if Kenobi never returned. Obi-Wan departed with Maul's corpse, speaking to Luke through the Force, assuring him that he would always be present; if not in person, then in spirit. ====Demolition games==== [[File:MaulOnTatooine-Demolition.jpg|right|thumb|Darth Maul competing in Jabba's demolition games]] {{Quote|None shall survive.|Darth Maul|[[Star Wars: Demolition: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars: Demolition'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]}} Maul was somehow once more alive on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], sometime shortly after the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]. Before anyone had even seen him, the young [[Wade Vox]] felt his presence in the Force as a strange, prickling sense of fear as he was getting ready for combat in [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba's]] [[Jabba's demolition games|demolition games]]; this feeling stayed with him throughout the combat, though Vox tried to shake off the feeling of impending dread after his narrow victory. It was soon after this that Jabba, floating over the Dune Sea and awaiting the next round of combat, spotted Maul's [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bike]] on the horizon. Jabba lifted his arm to point at the object in the distance and his suspicions were soon confirmed by [[Bib Fortuna/Legends|Bib Fortuna]] who informed his master that what he saw seemed to be a contraption favored by the Sith. Jabba let out a long, rumbling laugh and soon managed to convince Maul to take part in his demolition games so that Jabba could exploit his new "wild card" to gather even more ill-gotten gains.
